item.title: 84 days, four titles, one historic feat - Alcaraz's remarkable return
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

84 days, four titles, one historic feat - Alcaraz's remarkable return

The men's tennis season ended as it began, with a beaming Carlos Alcaraz holding aloft one of the sport's biggest trophies.

In January, he won the Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam. Ten months later, he stood as the victor in Turin, having ended his wait for a first ATP Finals title.

Watching Alcaraz over recent weeks, it would be easy to forget that for a four-month period this year, the 23-year-old barely picked up a racquet.

He missed the majority of the clay and all of the grass-court season with a wrist injury, but he has made a remarkable return, culminating in a dismantling of world number one Alexander Zverev on Sunday.

It is 84 days since Alcaraz made his comeback at the US Open, where his lack of match fitness understandably showed. He came through the early rounds but lost a five-set quarter-final epic against Ben Shelton.

Since then, the Spaniard has won 21 of his 22 matches - including each of the past 14 - and captured titles at four of the five tournaments he has contested.

He continues to make history, too, becoming the youngest man to win all four Slams and the season-ending Finals.

This was the third straight tournament he has won, following victories at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters earlier in November, and he has now won his past nine matches against fellow top-10 players.

The former world number one, currently ranked third behind Zverev and Jannik Sinner, continues to make up for lost time as he seeks to quickly reassert himself at the top of the sport.

"I think everybody feels he's the number one," Alcaraz said, stressing each player in the game has to treat themselves that way.

"Me, Sascha [Zverev], Jannik [Sinner], [Ben] Shelton. Having that confidence in yourself is really important.

"But right now the number one is Sascha. He really deserves it."

- Alcaraz outplays Zverev for first ATP Finals triumph

Crowd-pleasing variety, devastating power and astonishing athleticism did not take long to return to Alcaraz's game.

Even with a heavily strapped left leg after injuring his hamstring on Wednesday, he could not be stopped by the world's top players in Turin.

That included Zverev, who this year rose to the top of the rankings for the first time after claiming his first two major titles and recording a tour-leading 69 match wins.

Alcaraz, already a seven-time Slam winner, feels his own growth in the mental side of the sport has taken him to a different level in recent months.

He has specifically pointed to the new sense of perspective he gained from his time away from tennis in inspiring his scintillating year-end form.

"The injury made me realise what's really important," Alcaraz said.

"It's not winning. It's just about playing tennis. I realised that it is a gift every time that I can step on the court and compete healthy.

"When you realise that, everything comes easier.

"I don't feel stressed most of the time. I think right now I'm more mature, or I feel that, on a tennis court, I'm facing the problems and difficult moments in a different way."

Alcaraz threw himself to the ground after ending his wait to win the season-ending tournament before racing into the stands to celebrate with his team and family.

It marked the 30th title of his career, drawing him level with rival Sinner and behind only men's record 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic (102) among active ATP players.

More could soon be around the corner - should he manage to stay injury-free.

Victory in Paris has left him two titles away from emulating Sinner and Djokovic by completing the career 'Golden Masters' - winning all nine Masters 1,000 events, the level of tournament below the Slams.

Should he achieve that next season in Canada and Shanghai, it would leave him only an Olympic singles gold away from completing the sport.

His main obstacle to achieving such dominance still appears to be Sinner, given Alcaraz's positive head-to-head against Zverev.

Italian Sinner has been absent with a knee issue since Wimbledon but is aiming to return, external at the Australian Open, where Alcaraz will defend his title in January.

"In today's final, I needed to put the three Cs - cabeza, corazon, cojones - that my grandpa always tells me I have to give every time I step on the court," Alcaraz said.

"The three Cs in English is head, heart and balls. Today, that was what it was about.

"Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me."

Qatar GP 2026: Dates, schedule, weather, UK start time and how to watch or stream F1 race at Lusail International Circuit live on Sky Sports

Find out the race-week schedule, weather and how to watch the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit; watch every session live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday

Sunday 22 November 2026 19:38, UK

Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the last two rounds of the 2026 season with the Qatar Grand Prix hosting the penultimate event this weekend.

After a dramatic Las Vegas Grand Prix which saw 34 lead changes and Max Verstappen pull off a defensive masterclass, the F1 circus has moved to Qatar and the high-speed Lusail International Circuit.

Verstappen, who is set to finish runner-up in the Drivers' Championship behind Kimi Antonelli, won in Qatar last year after McLaren made a poor strategy call when in position for a one-two.

- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column

Like last year, there is a tyre limit which will create a minimum two-stop race with no driver allowed to do more than 27 laps on a set of tyres in the 50-lap race on Sunday.

This is due to the heavy loads which the tyres are put through in the fast corners which come one after another. The combination of this and this year's 2026 cars could create another fascinating race, particularly with high tension at the front between Mercedes and Red Bull as Verstappen and George Russell's rivalry escalated in Las Vegas.

Qualifying on Saturday is at 6pm UK time with the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday at 4pm, all live on Sky Sports F1.

Qatar GP track - Lusail International Circuit

The 3.367-mile Lusail International Circuit joined the F1 schedule in 2021 and is one of the highest speed tracks on the calendar due to its fast, flowing corners which punish the tyres but also makes following the car in front difficult.

In the first four editions of the event, which took place when DRS was still in use, most of the overtakes came at Turn One where drivers can make moves on the outside and inside, so it will be interesting to see whether the 2026 regulations create any additional opportunities.

Qatar GP weather

As usual in Qatar, there is no rain forecast across the three days of F1 action with temperatures at around 26C for Qualifying on Saturday and the race on Sunday.

item.title: 'This cannot continue'.- Ferrari to hold fresh Leclerc-Hamilton talks after collision
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clashes 'cannot continue' after Las Vegas GP with Frederic Vasseur to speak to drivers again

Sunday 22 November 2026 17:03, UK

Ferrari team boss Frederic Vasseur says he will hold further discussions with drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their latest tangle in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, admitting such incidents "cannot continue".

After costly clashes in Monza and Mexico City earlier this season, the Ferrari drivers came together when battling over sixth place with 12 laps to go on the Strip circuit in a race dominated by slip-streaming in which the leading runners were covered by a handful of seconds for most of the race.

Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton with a move down the inside of Turn Seven but made contact with the Briton, who was spun around. Stewards found Leclerc at fault and handed him a 10-second penalty, which dropped him to 10th place. Hamilton finished seventh.

In an unusually-strongly worded statement in Ferrari's post-race press release, Vasseur said: "For the second time in three races, something unacceptable has happened between our drivers, and this cannot continue.

"We sent a very clear message to both drivers in Brazil, and today during the race we told them to think about the team when racing each other.

"Of course, in this kind of race you cannot freeze the positions because, with the slipstream, if you slow down, the car behind will overtake you.

"But our drivers should have handled the situation differently, as other team-mates did both in front of and behind them.

"Charles knows he made a mistake and apologised, but that doesn't change the result."

Speaking to the written media after the race, Vasseur had said: "All the other teams, they were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race.

"[Kimi] Antonelli-[George] Russell, [Oscar] Piastri-[Lando] Norris, even Isack [Hadjar] overtook Max [Verstappen].

"Honestly, you can't imagine the frustration for me but, for more importantly, for all the guys at the [team]."

What will happen next?

The situation is increasingly frustrating for Vasseur given it was only three weeks ago that he had to resolve the fallout from a first-lap battle between the drivers that likely cost the team a one-two result in Mexico.

Vasseur brought Hamilton and Leclerc together to speak four days later ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, a meeting he said had "cleared the situation" and acted as "a good reset on the mindset" ahead of that weekend. The Frenchman added that they even "left my room joking together".

Immediately after Sunday's race in Las Vegas, the Ferrari team principal held an initial conversation with Leclerc having asked the Monegasque driver to see him before anything else.

Asked afterwards what they had talked about, Vasseur said: "It was not a discussion, I spoke!

"He apologised, he understands, but the result is there. That you do a mistake, you say 'it's my mistake, I'm sorry' but you did a mistake."

Asked what would happen next, Vasseur said: "I want to digest tonight [after the race] and we'll have to sit down tomorrow with both of them and to take a decision."

He added: "I want, once again, to have a discussion tomorrow. Also Charles will digest the situation and I think it's not the right place to discuss with them two minutes after the race.

"I saw Charles a bit down and I told him what I wanted to say but I'd prefer to discuss with him tomorrow about it."

'It's not a matter of rules' - Vasseur insists 'respect' the key between team-mates

The Las Vegas incident has placed renewed focus on what Vasseur will do to try and bring his drivers definitively into line, with scrutiny growing on whether Ferrari will follow the lead of other teams, such as McLaren and Mercedes, and introduce more formal 'rules of engagement' for what is allowed when in team-mate combat.

Hamilton has called for clearer policies in recent months and said after Sunday's race that "hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out".

Vasseur, however, believes the chaotic nature of Sunday's race shows that clean driving between team-mates is all about respect rather than predefined agreements.

"Honestly, it's not a matter of rules," insisted Vasseur.

"What can you do differently except that you have to respect your team-mate? In this kind of race you have to overtake the car who is in front of you. You can't stay behind, it's completely unmanageable.

"It means you just have to do it with respect when it's your team-mate, to take less risk, perhaps to come side by side and to come back behind. But you can't put it on the paper. I think the race of today [Sunday] nobody would write a scenario like this. Nobody can imagine a race like this. It means they just have to act in a professional way.

"Today it was unprofessional."

Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the Qatar Grand Prix with live coverage from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW

item.title: WRU to discuss Anglo-Welsh move at crucial summit
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

WRU to discuss Anglo-Welsh move at crucial summit

Welsh Rugby Union chief executive (WRU) Abi Tierney says the prospect of Welsh clubs joining an expanded English league will be discussed in January at a crucial two-day summit meeting.

The event, which has been delayed after initially being planned for December, will include the WRU, regions and external stakeholders - with plans to cut a Welsh professional men's side also to be discussed.

"The summit is critical and we're creating it together," said Tierney, speaking after the WRU annual general meeting (AGM) at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

"It is everything. We'll have all the owners and their boards in a room, all the data and facts on the table, and we'll be saying, this is what it tells us."

The WRU announced they hope for both internal and external speakers, with three key areas set to be focused on; financial and commercial, pathways and performance, and what it takes to win.

Anglo-Welsh options emerge but URC issues remain

Tierney admitted the recent prospect of trying to get into an Anglo-Welsh league will be discussed in January.

Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney confirmed earlier in November that the WRU had officially asked to join the English Prem and form an Anglo-Welsh league.

The Prem hopes to expand from 10 to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season, with a "long-term ambition" to grow further.

Prem Rugby has opened a registration process for teams to apply, with a 'request for information stage' now open until 1 February 2027 and which Welsh sides will now consider applying for.

Tierney was careful about what she said as she addressed the issue for the first time.

"Clearly, there's been a significant change in something that wasn't there a year ago that we've got to now take into account," she said.

"When we originally did the consultation last year, Anglo-Welsh wasn't an option. We tested it at the time and were told it wasn't an option.

"We've always said through this process that if other things change and options become available, it's beholden on us to explore all options.

"We've got a lot of water to go under the bridge to figure out what that combination is."

That includes discussions on continued involvement in the United Rugby Championship (URC), the five-country, cross-border competition to which the WRU is committed to providing four sides until 2028.

The WRU are a stakeholder in the competition alongside other member unions from Scotland, Ireland, Italy and South Africa.

"The relationship with the URC continues to be constructive," said Tierney.

"We're talking to them regularly. I think they understand on a human and inter-relational level. We continue to work as we always have."

When asked whether there was any threat of legal action towards the WRU, Tierney replied: "Yes, I think they'll be looking to make sure their interpretation of the contract, that we're clear on that. But we're going through that process."

Is three clubs still the magic number?

Whether any Anglo-Welsh involvement affects the number of Welsh men's clubs that are retained remains to be seen.

The WRU has said it intends to drop a professional men's side by 2028.

With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales.

That decision is expected to be made in July 2027 with the summit outlining how the choice will be made.

Tierney was challenged at the AGM on the three-team plan that was unveiled in October 2025, while Ospreys and Scarlets have condemned the plan, saying Welsh rugby should keep four sides.

She responded that the WRU had not heard another plan, although she and director of rugby and head of elite performance Dave Reddin both stated they "were open to other options".

"If you read the consultation documents and responses to the consultation, everybody agreed radical change was needed and the majority agreed reducing the number of clubs," said Tierney.

"It's hard when the impact is real and it becomes one club.

"If you want a consensus, the only thing you're potentially going to have is continuing to do the same thing. I don't think that is going to put Wales on a sustainable footing."

Tierney says she is not giving up on trying to find a solution at the rugby summit.

"We've always said our preference would be to do this via consensus but if we can't get it, that doesn't mean we shouldn't do what we believe is our job as a national governing body," said Tierney.

"To do the right thing for the whole of Welsh rugby, as opposed to what's right for individual parts."

- WRU publishes data on why west Wales team will be cut

- Published9 October

- Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams

- Published13 November

WRU bosses grilled at robust AGM

The number of clubs was just one issue that the WRU hierarchy were grilled on, in one of the most robust AGM's in recent memory.

Tierney was asked about whether she thought support would improve in west Wales if a region was cut.

When she suggested concentrating talent and resources could mean more successful clubs that attract support, she was labelled as "naive".

A question was also asked whether there would be more money for each of the three remaining sides.

The four regions currently get Â£6.5m each from the WRU with Â£26m given in total.

That overall figure will be reduced by Â£6m to Â£20m because of the current financial situation, which means a move to a three-club system will see each organisation having Â£6.7m each, just Â£200,000 more than the current amount the four teams get.

Tierney was faced with a question about the internal culture within the WRU and whether its own staff have confidence in the governing bodyâs executive leadership.

She also chose not to respond to a query about comments made by former president and Welsh rugby legend Sir Gerald Davies, who criticised the current WRU leadership in the aftermath of the victory against New Zealand.…

item.title: ‘No doubt’: AB de Villiers makes fresh Australian ball-tampering claim
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

AB de Villiers claims he is certain Australia tampered with the ball as far back as the first Test of their infamous 2018 series in South Africa.

The former South Africa batter was in the middle when Cameron Bancroft was caught by TV cameras using sandpaper in the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town.

Bancroft, Usman Khawaja and Chadd Sayers have all alleged sandpaper was used to tamper with the ball in the second Test at Gqerberha, formerly Port Elizabeth.

De Villiers set up South Africa’s six-wicket win in that Test to level the series at 1-1 with an unbeaten century in the first innings.

After biting his tongue during the unfolding drama, South Africa’s fourth highest Test run-scorer has entered the fray to say he has “no doubt” Australia’s premeditated cheating began even earlier.

“It started in Durban, by the way, not in PE [Port Elizabeth],” the 42-year-old said on his YouTube channel on Monday. “We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time.

“Way too early for anyone to reverse a ball at Kingsmead. Trust me, I’ve played a lot of cricket there. So whatever they did there, whether it was sandpaper or nails ... I don’t care. The fact of the matter is they were caught and everyone knew.”

In his memoir, Sabr, Khawaja wrote that all players were aware of Australia’s ball tampering in Cape Town, and his claims have been supported by Bancroft, Sayers and David Warner.

That version was rejected as “nonsense” by now-captain Pat Cummins, who was backed by fellow quick Josh Hazlewood. In 2021 the bowling group from the Cape Town Test issued a joint statement denying any prior knowledge that sandpaper had been taken onto the field to tamper with the ball during the South Africa tour.

De Villiers suggested it was implausible Australia’s bowlers were not aware, and was critical of their denials about the use of sandpaper on the field.

“Why are we all so worried about the object that was used?” he said. “The fact of the matter is there was a premeditated decision made to do something illegal on the ground.

“And every single person knew about it. I have zero per cent doubt about it.”

Cricket Australia declined to comment when contacted by Guardian Australia.

His most scathing criticism, however, was reserved for Cricket Australia’s handling of the fallout, and the team’s decision not to take collective responsibility at the time.

De Villiers said it was “absolutely ridiculous” Warner, Bancroft and then captain Steve Smith were left to take the hit and argued their suspensions were excessive.

“Cricket Australia needs to take the blame and not so much the players because they [CA] didn’t deal with it in the right manner,” he said. “It became a political thing. The prime minister [Malcolm Turnbull] got involved.

“The players obviously panicked. They were emotional ... I just feel they should have stuck together as a unit. They threw the guys under the bus and forced a situation like this to pop up again eight years later.”

De Villiers pointed to ball-tampering scandals of the 1990s involving England’s Michael Atherton and former South African captain Hansie Cronje as examples that were dealt with better.

Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis was also found guilty by the ICC of ball tampering in 2013 and 2016, but was fined instead of suspended.

De Villiers admitted he wasn’t a “beautiful angel” over his career, but said he only engaged in legal methods to foster reverse swing, such as bouncing the ball on the pitch on return throws.

“We try and push the boundaries as much as possible,” he said. “We all have tried over the years to get the ball to do something to get an edge, but obviously not being as stupid as to take an object on to the field and blatantly cheating.”

Source: The Guardian Sport | Published: 2026-11-23 03:47 UTC

item.title: Dylan Larkin trade grades in Red Wings-Canadiens blockbuster
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

The longstanding impasse between Dylan Larkin and the Detroit Red Wings ended on Sunday with a stunning trade to the Montreal Canadiens.

Dylan Larkin trade grades in Red Wings-Canadiens blockbuster

A stunning trade is finally made.

It’s a major deal with a lot of moving parts, which includes picks, prospects, and established players — so here is the full deal.

Montreal Canadiens receive:

- C Dylan Larkin

- 2nd round pick (2028)

- 3rd round pick (2027)

Detroit Red Wings receive:

- F Kirby Dach

- G Samuel Montembault

- C Michael Hage (rights)

- 1st round pick (2027)

- 2nd round pick (2027)

- 4th round pick (2028)

- 1st round pick (2029)

It’s a mammoth deal, so let’s break this down from both sides.

Montreal Canadiens grade: B-

Larkin is a very good player who makes the Canadiens immediately better, but this is an extremely steep price for a guy who isn’t a point-per-game guy, and in a buyer’s market no less. Larkin’s trade value was plummeting, and Montreal ended up pulling the trigger early after going 5-3-2 in their last 10, and having significant consistency issues.

The good news for the Canadiens is that Larkin will slot into their second line and should really boost the play of Juraj Slafkovsky, whose goal-scoring and production have been in the toilet due to Montreal lacking a legitimate second-line distributor. On paper there are a lot of reasons this should work, but Larkin being mercurial really makes this a more iffy prospect.

One of his biggest gripes was wanting to play for a contender, which the Canadiens satisfied — but there were also undercurrents that he wanted to play on a team with his Team USA compatriots from the Olympics. Getting shipped to Montreal is about as far from that as imaginable, so there is a discernible powder keg situation where Larkin wanted to be dealt to the Wild or Devils, and ended up in a place he didn’t expect.

It’s combustible. This could really pay off, or it could backfire pretty spectacularly.

Detroit Red Wings grade: A+

This is a pretty major haul, but a lot of it is noise. Dach and Montembault are both … fine. Kirby Dach has never lived up to expectations, and it’s unrealistic to think that will dramatically change in Detroit. The real meat of this deal comes from the two first round picks, and the rights to Michael Hage.

I really love Hage as a pickup for Detroit. Currently playing for the University of Michigan, he has steadily improved over his three years at the school and has become a prospect to watch as a puck distributor. In 13 games for the Wolverines this season he’s posted 5 goals and 21 assists, which could indicate potential development into an elite center. The Canadiens couldn’t keep waiting, and their loss is Detroit’s gain here.

Adding those two first-round picks is a boon, even if they’re likely to come in the back half of the round, or potentially even at the end. The big stunner here is that the haul came through even though everything felt like the Wings were going to have to settle for a mediocre offer at the deadline just to offload their disgruntled star.

item.description:

The early games of Week 11 are winding down. It wasn’t the prettiest slate of games, but football games and stats were produced on a field with grass or some kind of turf covering that field. We’ve seen some ugly football today, but as teams lose players to injuries and start young players for evaluation, things get ugly.

Fantasy football waiver wire: Early Week 12 pickups

Justice Hill, Ted Hurst, and Caleb Douglas highlight the top early waiver wire fantasy football targets entering Week 12.

Week 12 Byes

None

Week 12 Waiver Wire Pickups

Late game update

Fernando Mendoza, Raiders, QB (18%)

Mendoza complete under 50% of his passes against the Broncos in Denver, but he also put up 267 yards three touchdowns and a pick-six to end the game. Three touchdown passes is pretty good, especially when you consider that Brock Bowers was unable to play.

How useful he’ll be in fantasy moving forward is hard to know, but he’s proving he can put up fantasy points with some average receivers. Getting Bowers back will be huge and having Ashton Jeanty breaking off huge catch and runs doesn’t hurt either.

Geno Smith, QB, Jets (18%)

Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday’s 27-24 win over the Chargers. He remains a streaming option at quarterback despite inconsistency. Next week he faces the Dolphins, who he put up 287 yards and three touchdowns against in Week 7.

Chimere Dike, WR, Tennessee Titans (13%)

Dike took over the slot role in Week 11 and ended up leading the team in receptions and yards, catching 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards. It wasn’t a huge fantasy game, but if he can keep that slot job, he should be set up for a good PPR floor moving forward.

Jack Bech, Raiders, WR (1%)

Fernando Mendoza appears to like wide receiver Jack Bech, as he’s targeted him on 25% of his passes through his first two games. This week Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for88 yards and a touchdown. This usage comes with Brock Bowers off the field for most of the time, but I do like that Mendoza likes him and if that keeps up next week with Bowers possibly back, we may be onto something.

Jacoby Brissett, QB, Ravens (21%)

Justice Hill, RB, Ravens (21%)

With Jacoby Brissett in as the Ravens quarterback, they are going to chuck the ball to finish out the season. In his two starts he’s thrown the ball 49 and 37 times. This isn’t your Lamar Jackson Ravens anymore, as he attempted 20, 20, 31, and 25 passes in his four full starts this year. Derrick Henry needs the threat of Jackson taking off as a runner to keep teams honest. Without that the Ravens aren’t going to force the run like they once did.

More passing is great for Zay Flowers and good for Brissett and running back Justice Hill. This week against the Panthers, Brissett completed 24-of-37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while running twice for seven yards. That’s not winning your league for you, but there is no-doubt upside there if you need help at QB.

Derrick Henry had a good game against the Panthers, rushing 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown, while catching four passes for 17 yards. Unfortunately he lost a fumble after one of those receptions and he appeared to have suffered a concussion late in the game on his 15-yard touchdown run. That could set up more touches for passing down back Hill next week against the Texans. This week he played well, rushing six times for 69 yards and a touchdown, while catching 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards. He also lost a fumble in the back of the end zone. He was so close to two touchdowns on the day.

Even if Henry doesn’t miss time, Hill is worth a pickup in this more pass oriented offense moving forward.

Ted Hurst, WR, Buccaneers (1%)

Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers were finally forced to throw the ball, and it didn’t go great, as they lost to the Lions, but that was likely. The good news is that Mayfield and company were able to put up some fantasy points through the air. The leader of the group ended up being Hurst, who led the team in targets, receptions, yards and touchdowns. He caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and a pair of touchdowns. We’ve seen Hurst show out in the past, but this looks like we could see him take over as WR1 if he can stay healthy. The Bucs really need someone to step up in the receiving game, and I like Hurst’s chances.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (46%)

Kyle McCord is not good. But, he is still targeting Douglas like a No. 1 wide receiver. This week he threw in his general direction 10 times, but only completed two passes for 30 yards to the rookie. The looks are there, but the connection isn’t. Next week the Dolphins get the Jets, who Douglas caught two touchdowns against last time they met in Week 7. If you are in a matchup next week that doesn’t look good for your team, get Douglas into your lineup for a shot at some offensive fireworks.
